newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WEST HAM SIGN STRIKER KITSON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEST HAM SIGN STRIKER KITSON.

text.p: Suffering premier league side West Ham United ended their long search for a striker on Thursday by signing Paul Kitson from Newcastle for 2.3 million pounds ($3.7 million), the club said.
The former Derby forward has been in talks with West Ham manager Harry Redknapp over the last week and had agreed personal terms.
Redknapp said: "We have been desperately short of a goalscorer - everybody can see that. But I am convinced we will get out of trouble and be a better team for it."
The Hammers' goal drought has seen them slip into the relegation zone. They are third from bottom and they crashed out of the F.A. Cup last month at the hands of second division Wrexham.
High-profile foreign signings such as Paolo Futre, Ilie Dumitrescu and Florin Raducioiu have all failed to make an impact.
Kitson, a former England under-21 striker, joined Newcastle from Derby for 2.25 million pounds ($3.6 million) in September 1994 but started only 26 league matches in 2-1/2 years at St James' Park.
The 26-year-old striker has been squeezed out of the scene by a series of foreign imports and has recently been missing from training and the substitutes bench.
Redknapp is believed to be searching for another striker, with Stoke's Mike Sheron and Clive Mendonca of Grimsby seen as his main targets.
